summary: Our project describes the journey of an aspiring space crew who have a system malfunction, and crash on Mars. Few survive, and face an unknown landscape. Miraculously, the vessel is still able to communicate with ground control. The goal of this game is to find out more about the Martian landscape and eventually get back to Earth.
details: Our game allows young children from ages 7-12 to explore what it feels like to be stranded on a Martian base, that is, managing resources, grappling with dust storms and solar storms (Which are much more common on Mars than Earth) and all the while trying to gather scientific information. Houston, We Have A Solution is a martian base simulation game where the player is stranded on Mars with very little resources and no communication back to Earth. It requires its players to complete research tasks that allow the player to develop technology to reach out to the operators waiting back at Earth to alert them of the player's dire situation. During this time, the player has to deal with weather events such as dust storms and solar storms, which take away the players health if they do not seek shelter immediately. The game also has accurate representations of both of the Moons of Mars: Deimos and Phobos. The orbits of the moons are synced with the in-game time and the player is able to look at the moons using the telescope experiment. There are quite a few more research tasks that are available to the user, such as: sifting through the Martian dirt to find different minerals such as Sulfur and organic compounds, looking at both the moons of Mars, looking at solar particles, and looking at a nearby crater to find ripples in the crater that indicates a dried-up lake. This has the benefit of challenges the young minds and strengthening their thinking skills via the simple-but-challenging resource management in Houston, We Have A Solution. After you complete a research experiment, you can get research points, and after you have 100 research points, you can contact Earth with a chance of being rescued. We made this app with the Scratch-based online IDE named Gandi IDE. Our project is creative since it introduces and simulates an idea that has never been simulated before, and does that in a novel and simple way so that it is understandable by 7-12 year olds. Our team considered our target audience and the real data from NASA.
